summary: gRPC unknown tokens queued without bound on the process-wide LEGACY_SCAN semaphore (gRPC had no failed-auth budget), so an unauthenticated gRPC flood locked REST legacy-key holders out
note: one gRPC failed-auth budget for all callers (60/min, Redis auth_fail_grpc) that skips only the legacy scan (401, no negative cache; Redis errors fail open), charged before the scan (W3R-08); gRPC scans take their own turn (ScanLane::Grpc), so a gRPC flood can delay only gRPC legacy keys; a turn still busy after the bounded wait is 503 / UNAVAILABLE, never 401 (W3R-07). The first fix (a flat 2 s wait on the shared turn, then 401; the budget read before the scan and charged after it) was reworked by W3R-07 and W3R-08. Legacy keys stay supported (10 active in production, operator decision)

summary: A valid legacy (lookup_hash IS NULL) key was refused with 401 with no attacker present: the flat 2 s wait for the process-wide scan turn was shorter than one scan of the 10 production legacy keys (~2.2-2.5 s at cost 12), so concurrent requests for the same dormant key gave up as busy (401, which SDKs do not retry) and were charged as failed auths; waiters that got the turn re-verified a stale candidate list
note: concurrent requests for one token on one lane share one scan (LegacyFlight; followers wait up to 20 s and are not charged); a request that waited for the turn re-checks the record cache, the negative cache and lookup_hash, then re-reads the candidates; the wait covers the larger of its own and the holder's scan at the measured verify speed + 1 s, capped at 10 s; a turn still busy is 503 with Retry-After: 5 on REST and /auth/login (gRPC UNAVAILABLE), never 401, never negatively cached or charged; the lookup_hash backfill is awaited. Tests: w3_auth_concurrent_requests_for_a_dormant_legacy_key_share_one_scan, w3_auth_legacy_key_behind_a_busy_scan_turn_is_503_with_retry_after

summary: The gRPC failed-auth budget did not protect REST: one failure held the process-wide scan turn for a whole scan, so one or two sequential gRPC clients with bogus tokens stayed under budget and kept the turn busy for REST legacy keys; concurrent requests all read the counter before any was charged, and cancelled requests were never charged
note: REST/login and gRPC scan on separate turns (bcrypt_gate::ScanLane); the budgets are charged before the scan (INCR, then compare: charge_failed_auth) and refunded (DECR) when the key is found or the scan never runs (turn busy, database error), so concurrency and client cancellation cannot bypass them and a burst for a dormant legacy key costs nothing; a record-cache or lookup_hash match is never charged or gated. Tests: w3_auth_legacy_scans_take_separate_turns_per_transport, w3_auth_failed_auth_budget_is_charged_before_the_scan
